explanation: The M230L substitution minimally destabilizes etravirine binding through a subtle loss of favorable van der Waals contacts rather than direct ligand interaction. Although leucine is only slightly smaller than methionine (3.8 Å³ volume reduction), the loss of methionine's sulfur atom—which can engage in favorable σ-hole interactions or marginal van der Waals contacts with the inhibitor at the 5.6 Å closest approach distance—eliminates a low-energy contribution to binding. The increased hydrophobicity of leucine may also slightly reorient the local pocket geometry in the fingers-palm subdomain, causing cumulative loss of optimal positioning rather than direct steric clash, explaining the negligible but detectable resistance phenotype.
